You hear a conversation between a GP and a patient about recurring
 diarrhoea.
 What does the GP ask the patient to confirm?
A. Whether she caught the disease in St Petersburgh, Russia.
B. Whether she was in the vicinity of a place with the disease
 recently.
C. Whether she had been to the tropics recently as the disease is
 common there.

You hear a physician in the A&E department talking with a patient
 presenting with abdominal pain.
 The physician wants to deal with the patient’s dehydration by...
A. Ordering an x-ray of the patient’s abdomen.
B. Having blood drawn in order to run tests.
C. Having an IV put in while other tests are run.

You hear a ward briefing about a newly admitted patient.
 What does the doctor conducting the briefing want to confirm?
A. The reason the patient is in pain.
B. The reason the condition was triggered.
C. The reason the patient’s eyes are sore.

You hear part of a training on communication between providers.
 What will be the priority of the new role discussed?
A. To improve communication between doctors and patients
B. To improve communication between patients and nurses
C. To improve communication between doctors and nurses.

You hear a trainee doctor discussing stress with a senior GP.
 What does the senior doctor identify as the cause of the problem in
 general practice?
A. The unwillingness of younger GPs to work locally or full time.
B. The number of doctors opting to go into general practice.
C. The difficulty with balancing the long days with family life.

You hear a conversation between a nurse and a doctor about
 scheduling appointments.

 Why did the nurse mention that she had already spent an hour on the
 task?
A. To show that she had already put in reasonable effort before
 asking for help.
B. To show that she does not have enough information to complete
 the task quickly.
C. To show that she is also feeling the effect of the hospital being
 short-handed at the moment.

The speaker points out that many of the foot conditions people suffer
 from…
A. Are more common among the elderly.
B. Do not necessitate medical intervention.
C. Can be dangerous if handled by someone without skill or knowledge.

What is the main purpose of the project?
A. To save money by empowering patients with minor conditions
B. To discharge as many patients as possible for the podiatry service
C. To focus all of the podiatry service’s efforts on high risk conditions

What types of patients were deemed suitable for self-care?
A. Those with high risk medical or podiatric needs
B. Those able to take care of low risk conditions
C. Those with a medically-trained family member

What was offered to patients considered to be low risk?
A. Small group educational sessions
B. One-to-one assessment appointments
C. Small group assessment sessions

How did the project result in cost savings?
A. By reducing the total number of patients seen by podiatrists
B. By reducing the number of podiatrists seeing patients
C. By reducing the number of appointments involving low risk patients

According to the speaker, the primary benefit to patients was…
A. The quality of care that podiatry patients received
B. The amount of time patients had to wait to be seen
C. The level of satisfaction of all podiatry patients

What is the current role of the interviewee?
A. A leader of an organization that works to promote nursing
B. A nurse with experience working with elderly patients
C. A health practitioner with a background in emergency medicine

According to the interviewee, what is causing the lack of physician
 integration?
A. The poor communications systems in place
B. The lack of permanent physicians at hospitals
C. The integrated care model recently adopted

Why was the interviewer surprised by the interviewee’s initial response
 about challenges?
A. Because he does not agree with what she has said.
B. Because he has information that contradicts what she said.
C. Because he has heard information about another problem.

According to the interviewee, what is the most serious result of short-
 staffing?
A. Job satisfaction and burnout of nurses
B. Significant turnover in health systems
C. Increased risks to patient safety

The interviewee notes that long hours can negatively affect…
A. The mental abilities of nurses
B. The physical abilities of nurses
C. The family and social life of nurses

What challenge does the interviewee say might be surprising to many?
A. Domestic violence
B. Bullying by physicians
C. Bullying by patients
